Proposition 2.3, Proposition 2.4: The KPZ fixed point formula its properties
nodes.statement:
For any $\mathfrak{h}_0\in\text{\upshape{UC}}$, the KPZ fixed point $t \mapsto \mathfrak{h}_t(\,\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\,; \mathfrak{h}_0)$ is a Feller process on $\text{\upshape{UC}}$, whose distribution function for any $t > 0$ and $\mathfrak{g} \in \text{\upshape{LC}}$ is given by the formula
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{\mathfrak{h}_0} \bigl( \mathfrak{h}_t(x) \le \mathfrak{g}(x),\, \forall\, x\in\mathbb{R}\bigr) = \det \Bigl(I - \mathbf{K}^{\text{\upshape{hypo}}(\mathfrak{h}_0)}_{t/2}\mathbf{K}^{\text{\upshape{epi}}(\mathfrak{g})}_{-t/2} \Bigr)_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}.
\end{equation}

Let $\mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{h}_0)$ denote the KPZ fixed point with initial data $\mathfrak{h}_0\in \text{\upshape{UC}}$. Then it has the following properties, where all of the identities in distribution are for random functions in the spatial variable on $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont{(\roman*)},ref=\roman*]
\item   \emph{(1:2:3 scaling invariance)} For any $\alpha>0$, one has $\alpha\hspace{0.05em}\mathfrak{h}_{\alpha^{-3}t}(\alpha^{-2}x; \mathfrak{h}^{\alpha}_0)\stackrel{\text{\upshape{\tiny{dist}}}}{=} \mathfrak{h}_t(x;\mathfrak{h}_0)$ as a process in both $x$ and $t$, where $\mathfrak{h}^\alpha_0(x) := \alpha^{-1}\mathfrak{h}_0(\alpha^{2}x)$.
\item  \emph{(Stationarity in space)} For any $t > 0$ and $u \in \mathbb{R}$, $\mathfrak{h}_t(x +u; \mathfrak{h}_0(\,\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\, -u))\stackrel{\text{\upshape{\tiny{dist}}}}{=} \mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{h}_0)$, where we write $\mathfrak{h}_0(\,\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\, -u)$ for the function $y \mapsto \mathfrak{h}_0(y -u)$.
\item  \emph{(Affine invariance)} Let $\mathfrak{f}(x) = \mathfrak{h}_0(x) + a + c x$ for some constants $a, c$. Then one has $\mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{f})\stackrel{\text{\upshape{\tiny{dist}}}}{=} \mathfrak{h}_t(x+\frac12ct; \mathfrak{h}_0) + a + cx + \frac14c^2t$ as a process in $x$ and $t$.
\item   \emph{(Skew time reversibility)} For any functions $\mathfrak{f},\mathfrak{g}\in\text{\upshape{UC}}$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\big(\mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{g})\le -\mathfrak{f}(x), \,\forall\,x \in \mathbb{R}\big) =\mathbb P\big(\mathfrak{h}_t(x;\mathfrak{f})\le -\mathfrak{g}(x), \,\forall\,x \in \mathbb{R}\big).
\end{equation}
\item  \emph{(Preservation of max)} For any $\mathfrak{f}_1,\mathfrak{f}_2\in\text{\upshape{UC}}$ and $t > 0$, the KPZ fixed points $\mathfrak{h}_t(\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\,; \mathfrak{f}_1)$ and $\mathfrak{h}_t(\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\,; \mathfrak{f}_2)$ can be coupled so that $\mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{f}_1)\vee \mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{f}_2) \stackrel{\text{\upshape{\tiny{dist}}}}{=} \mathfrak{h}_t(x;\mathfrak{f}_1\vee \mathfrak{f}_2)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
\item  \emph{(Monotonicity)} For any $t > 0$ and $\mathfrak{f}_1,\mathfrak{f}_2\in\text{\upshape{UC}}$ such that $\mathfrak{f}_1 \geq \mathfrak{f}_2$, the KPZ fixed points $\mathfrak{h}_t(\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\,; \mathfrak{f}_1)$ and $\mathfrak{h}_t(\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{\mathpalette{.5}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}}@{.5}\,; \mathfrak{f}_2)$ can be coupled so that $\mathfrak{h}_t(x;\mathfrak{f}_1) \geq \mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{f}_2)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ a.s.\
\item  \emph{($\tfrac{1}{2}^{{\scriptscriptstyle-}}-$H\"older regularity in space)} For any fixed $t>0$ and $\beta\in (0,\tfrac12)$, the function $x \mapsto \mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{h}_0)$ is almost surely locally $\beta$-H\"{o}lder continuous.
\item  \emph{($\tfrac{1}{3}^{{\scriptscriptstyle-}}$-H\"older regularity in time)} For any fixed $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\beta\in (0,\tfrac13)$, the function $t \mapsto \mathfrak{h}_t(x; \mathfrak{h}_0)$ is almost surely locally $\beta$-H\"{o}lder continuous.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{h}_0:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ satisfy Assumption~1.1 and suppose that $A>0$. There exist $L_0$ and $c'>0$ (both depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $A$) such that, for all $L> L_0$, there exists $n_0$ (depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $L$) so that for all $n>n_0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,

$$\mathbb P\left(\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}\in\mathsf{TP}_{\!\!A,L}^{\varepsilon}\right) \geq c'\varepsilon.$$

Further, $L_0$ and $c'$ may be taken to depend continuously on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $A$.

Let $\mathfrak{h}_0:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ satisfy Assumption~1.1 and suppose  $A>0$. There exist $c' >0$ and $L_0>0$ (both depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $A$) such that, for all $L>L_0$, there exists $n_0$ (depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $L$) such that, for all $n>n_0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,


$$\mathbb P\bigg(\sup_{x\in[x_0^{n}+A,x_0^{n}+A+2]}\!\!\!\! \mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}(x) > \mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}(x_0^{n}) - \varepsilon;\,\,  |\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}(x_0^{n})| \leq \beta L^{1/2};\,\,  |x_0^{n}|\leq \beta L-A-2\bigg) \geq c'\varepsilon,$$

where $x_0^{n} = arg\,max_{|x|\leq n^{1/60}} \mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}(x)$ and is taken to be the largest (i.e., not necessarily greatest in absolute value) one on the event that it is not unique; we will use shorthand $\smash{x_0=x_0^{n}}$ below at times. Further, $L_0$ and $c'$ can be taken to depend on $\gamma,$ $\theta,$ and $A$ continuously.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.6: Uniform tail bounds for BrLPP from LPPtools
nodes.statement:
There exist finite positive constants $n_0$, $K_0$, $C$, and~$c$ such that, for $n\geq n_0$, $K_0\leq K \leq n^{1/30}$, and $0<R < n^{1/46}$,

$$\mathbb P\left(\sup_{x,y\in[-R,R]} \left|\mathcal{S}_n(y, x) + (y-x)^2\right| > K\right) \leq CR^2\exp(-cK^{3/2}).$$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.7: Location of maximizer
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{h}_0:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ satisfy Assumption~1.1 .
Let $x_0^{n}$ be the maximizer of $\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}$ of largest absolute value. Given $\delta>0$, there exist $n_0$ and $M<\infty$ (both depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $\delta$) such that, for all $n\geq n_0$,

$$\mathbb P\left(|x_0^{n}| > M\right) \leq \delta.$$

Further, $M$ can be taken to depend on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $\delta$ continuously.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.16: Positive prob of favourable data
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{h}_0:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ satisfy Assumption~1.1 and consider $A>0$. There exist $K$ and $L_0$ (both depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $A$) such that, for all $L>L_0$, there exists $n_0$ (depending on $\gamma$, $\theta$, and $L$) so that, for all $n>n_0$,

$$\mathbb P(\mathsf{Fav}_{K,L}) \geq \frac{1}{2}.$$

Further, $K$ and $L_0$ may be made to depend on $\gamma$, $\theta$ and $A$ in a continuous manner.

Lemma 5.11, Lemma 5.12: Properties of reconstruction of…
nodes.statement:
For each upright path $\gamma$ starting on line $n$ and ending on  line $1$, the process $z \mapsto \mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)},z}(\gamma)$ is non-increasing almost surely; or constant almost surely; or non-decreasing almost surely. Moreover, it is an almost sure event that:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item if $-n^{1/60}\leq x\leq x_0+A$, then $\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)},z}(x) = \mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)}}(x)$ for all $z\in \mathbb{R}$; and
  \item if $x\geq x_0+A+2$, then $\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)},z}(x)$ is non-increasing in $z$.
\end{enumerate}

It holds almost surely that, for any $z_1, z_2\in \mathbb{R}$,

$$\left|\sup_{x\in [x_0+A,x_0+A+ 2]}\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)},z_1}(x) - \sup_{x\in[x_0+A,x_0+A+ 2]}\mathfrak{h}^{{\scriptscriptstyle(}n{\scriptscriptstyle)},z_2}(x)\right| \leq 2 |z_1-z_2|.$$
